utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, because I have to ask you the following: Should I consider that everything you said is correct and reliable?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to pause, both of us. Tell us, please, did you have veterans' service recognised?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From which date to which date?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think from 1992 until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 17th of April, 1992, until which date 1995?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 17th of April is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did you become a soldier of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, first of all the Territorial Defence and then the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which -- in which village in?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Suceska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, this puzzles me a bit, on the basis of your previous statements, I have this information to the effect that you were in a different municipality until the 25th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: A different municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were a soldier of the Territorial Defence of Suceska, which later became -- or, rather, grew into the 281st Light Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the commander of that brigade was -- you tell me who.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Zulfo Tursunovic; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he a trained officer?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you given a few statements in Bosnia-Herzegovina, first once in Bosnia-Herzegovina, then to the investigators of the OTP, then to the state commission, and then once again to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did it come about that in your statements given to Bosnian authorities you failed to mention you had been an active soldier?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: They did not ask me. And it was not my duty, strictly speaking, to give them a statement at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And when you were giving a statement to the OTP investigators, was the interview attended by anyone else from the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was present at that interview?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 65 ter 22378 without broadcasting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the last line here listing the present: [In English] "Names of all persons present during interview." [Interpretation] You don't have to read, but do you see this line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which capacity -- in fact, did you provide this statement requesting protective measures? Has your request for protective measures been standing all this time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement here as a suspect or as a victim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Where [as interpreted] was this statement given?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 20th of August, 1996. You speak English. Look at it. It will be clear.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give your statement as a suspect or as a victim? Did anyone tell you you were a suspect?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Suspected of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just asking. So you spoke to them as a victim.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Of course a victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what capacity were these two men present at the interview?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know who these people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have a consultation with any official in Bosnia-Herzegovina related to providing a statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your position at the time? You were rather young, weren't you, when you joined the army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. I was holding a position on the front line. We were on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Srebrenica became a protected area, elderly men were demobilised and then the brigade was diminished from 1 .400 to several hundred soldiers.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that those who were older were then demobilised when Srebrenica became a protected area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: When that happened, there was no army. All the weapons were taken away. It became a protected area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this brigade of -- commanded by Zulfo Tursunovic did not exist during the protected area period?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who prevented then the UNPROFOR from entering the so-called Bandera Triangle that was controlled by this brigade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How were you equipped while you were in the unit, if you had any equipment in terms of weapons, equipment, boots, ammunition?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We were not. I didn't have a weapon. I didn't have a uniform. I didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What were you wearing on the front line, your own clothes?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the actions and operations carried out by this unit from the enclave before the protected area period and during that period?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation, just so you know why I'm making a pause. Were you part of that unit on January 23rd?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: 23rd January. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you take part in the attack by that unit against Kravica on Christmas Day 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just to clarify the 23 January reference, perhaps that should have a year.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] January 1993. It's the year 1993, the whole year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come you were absent from the unit on the day of that attack?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I just didn't go into action anywhere. I don't know. I didn't even know about that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you find out later about that operation in Kravica and the attack against the Serbs on Christmas Day 1993?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know about other operations before the protected area period and during that period? Did you know about the operations undertaken within the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You didn't take part in any of these attacks?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any commendation as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your military service as a war veteran was recognised from day one to the last day; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This 281st Bosnian Light Brigade, how many platoons and companies did it have?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what battalion did you serve?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I know Zulfo was the chief commander. I don't know any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know who your direct commander was of your platoon, company, battalion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know any commanding officer or commander apart from Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I know that Naser was in Srebrenica, and who else was there, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who gave you your daily assignments in the field?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Nobody. We had to go to the front line every day. We had to be there every day and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where was the line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: On the hill behind the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll skip that then. You didn't hear about those excursions into Visnjica in June 1995, the attack on the Serbian village of Visnjica, the killing and burning of civilians?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go into private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in open session, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go straight to July 1995. You were still recorded as a member of the 281st Brigade and that's why your veteran status was recognised. Is it the case that in the Tolimir case you were shown a document drafted by the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH Army and a brief by General Delic dated 16 June? 1D5023 is the document I'd like to call up. Until then, Witness, you mentioned Jaglici. Is that close to Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before moving into the breakthrough, did everyone rejoin their brigade in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this, please. This is 16 July 1995, Rasim Delic, army commander.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we see page 3. Could we zoom in on item 3 for the witness. It says: "The units of the 28th Division are pulling out of Srebrenica and fighting their way out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have it, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Towards the top, number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Units of the 28th Division are pulling out of Srebrenica and fighting their way out. They have remained compact. They have scored success after success in the temporarily occupied territory. They have inflicted great losses on the aggressor. So far, they have eight Chetniks in captivity alive. Units of the 28th Division have linked up with the infiltrated units of the 2nd Corps. Their joint forces have continued fighting in the temporarily occupied territory. It's expected they will fully link up with these units. Activities are underway to exploit the successor units carrying out the breakthrough." So your commander says that you have restructured, that you are still compact, and that there was fighting by you together with the units of the 2nd Corps. Was there any fighting on your way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Not that I have seen. From Jaglici to Kasaba where I was taken prisoner, I did not see any fighting anywhere. We were just beaten by the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were these serious attacks by the Serbian troops?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Of course they were. They shelled us the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in one place you saw about 300 dead soldiers of the BH Army? Don't you think that some Serb troops were also killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. It was an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that 300 fighting men were killed, and do you know at least one of those names?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know any names. Those were not fighters. Those were civilians. I didn't see any soldiers with rifles there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D -- can this document be admitted first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, again the citation to, You saw 300 dead soldiers of the BH Army, can I have a citation to that? It doesn't match what I'm looking at in his prior statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking Mr. Karadzic for the citation. Can I ask the witness whether he saw about 300 dead soldiers or civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the previous document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember having seen a similar document, but in any event, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D5051, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5012, please. I apologise to Mr. Mitchell. If the witness had confirmed I would not have called up the document, it would have saved some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I've found the citation now, Mr. President. It's in another statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your statement which you provided on the 20th of July, one week after the events; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is probably something the witness can deal with, but I think Mr. Karadzic should take another look at the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this not be broadcast. First of all, it should be changed. 20th July, 2006. I apologise. And now can we go to the next page, page2. In Serbian it is the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "From there, we set out in the direction of Pobudska Kamenica where we joined up with one part of the first group, the Chetniks surrounded us and opened fire at us, and there were over 300 killed and a significant number of wounded. " What happened to those who were killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: They just stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the wounded? Did you manage to save them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that they started carrying them, but there was another round of shelling and they were left behind after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it is possible that some of those wounded also died?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who buried them and where?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did General Mladic have those wounded in mind when he said that he would send somebody out to assist them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2052 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After leaving Susnjari, you split into two groups. How come you went in the direction of Jaglici or whatever the name of that place is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Well, I heard from -- from other people that they were heading towards Susnjari and that they were proceeding towards Tuzla from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you heard that on the 10th or the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It was on the 11th of July that I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the 11th of July, you set out at what time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: In the afternoon. It was already dark when I arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the civilians? What were they supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: They were supposed to head towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did some members of your family go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. My father, my brother, my wife, everybody went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How old was your father at that time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Fifty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And your brother?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Fifteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You stated that you did not dare go to Potocari, that you were afraid. Was that because you were a soldier?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, I was not a soldier. They would have killed me like they did everybody else who went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come you were not a soldier? You were recognised as a soldier from the 17th of April until 1995.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It was a protected area, so that was recognised but it was not up to me. It was not my doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you split into two groups. Who commanded? Who issued the order to split the column into two a groups?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know who did that. When I joined them it was already dark. There was a huge field full of people, some 15.000 people, and I heard shouts that we should form a column. I spent the entire night there, and then we set out on the following day. I don't know exactly who it was who ordered us to form columns, how that came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the other column? Did they also attack and suffered losses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: What column are you talking about? It was one and only column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in your statement you said that you joined up the other part of the column.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the statement again. And then the second page again. You say here that there were markings telling you that the fields were mined. Who placed those marks? Was it Tursunovic who ordered somebody to do that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "By Kamenica where we gathered together with some people from the first group, and that's where they were attacked by the Chetniks." In other words, there were two groups; right? And you joined near Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It's a misunderstanding. A group that headed out before me stopped there and rested there. We caught up with them, and that's when we were surrounded, where fire was opened at us from an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Zulfo Tursunovic was at the head of the column together with armed men and that the back of the column was secured by Golic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, I did not see Zulfo Tursunovic, and I never heard about him while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. We have clarified that. We can move on. You said that on the 11th, you were told that able-bodied men should go to Jaglici; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How were you dressed? How were you equipped? Did you wear layers? Was it in keeping with the season of the year or differently? Did you wear a uniform? Did you have several trousers, pairs of trousers, on you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I -- I put on what I had. I could not go shopping before I set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it hot?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Of course it was hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many ambushes did you encounter, and how many times were you attacked by artillery?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: As soon as we set out from Jaglici we hit an and bush, and as far as shelling's concerned, that lasted all the time. There was a major ambush near Kamenica where we suffered about 300 dead and a significant number of injured, and then the fourth time where I was captured near Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that some people were killed by the falling trees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that the ambush near Kamenica was the second ambush and that it happened around 6.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last answer, because your answer was so quick the interpreters couldn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was the second ambush, and the first one was somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It was not a major ambush. They just opened fire at us. They came close to us and they opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did many people die as a result of artillery fire, the constant artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I was in the column. I could see dead people lying around in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please bear with me. I would like to skip a few things. I simply have to do that because of the time. Help us understand. You continued walking towards Nova Kasaba; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the 13th in the morning you were captured.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please make a break. I'll do the same. How many of you were there when you were captured?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you also saw some dead people in that place.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were taken to the school in Nova Kasaba; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then some 20 minutes later you were given some water; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were no UN soldiers anywhere near?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Serbian soldiers took care of your wounded. They tended to their wounds; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were sent to the football pitch. When was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Around 2.00 it says here; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We stayed there until the evening, perhaps an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did General Mladic appear?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when. When I arrived there, perhaps an hour or an hour and a half later he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between 3.00 and 4.00; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And how long was his speech, General Mladic's speech?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He said, did he not, that you were not criminals, that you would be exchanged? Did he or somebody else mention an offer for you to join Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: He did not say that we were not criminals. He said that they were not criminals. And as for Fikret Abdic, I never heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Mladic said that he wanted to send patrols through the forest to collect the wounded and to bury the dead according to the instructions of their families; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the end of his speech did Mladic ask for a list of the detainees to be made?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What happened to the list?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I believe that he took it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. How many of you were there at the football stadium?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I believe that there must have been about 2- or 3.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The number keeps growing, Witness. So far there was about 1.500. All of a sudden there's 2- to 3.000.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So their names could be listed so quickly that Mladic could take it with him.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. It didn't happen that fast, and I didn't claim for a fact that he did. I said that I believed that he did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we now look at the booklet -- or, rather, Mr. Ruez's book. I believe that what I want to show the witness is 242. [In English] May I ask the Prosecution to lend me once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 4308.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. This is not the right one. I'm interested in the stadium, the -- the football pitch in Nova Kasaba. That's what I want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 26 to 30. Probably you wanted to see page 28.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. Thank you. Twenty-eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this the football pitch we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where were you in this group, in which part of the group?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I believe somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who are the people standing in front of the group?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: You believe -- you mean here in the -- at the front of the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these detainees or Serbian soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when you started walking, did you start walking all together?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did you go from here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We were loaded onto buses and then in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw some four or five buses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We no longer need the photo. You say that you were transported to Bratunac; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not have a seat on the bus. You had to stand; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were standing in the middle of the bus; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour before dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the driver switched on the lights on the bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the lights in the bus? Were they on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How tall are you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: 5.5 foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Five feet.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 5.5. Okay. And you say that the bus was full. How could you see something through the window of such a full bus as you were standing in the middle?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Well, you know how high the windows on the bus are, you can see through them when you're sitting down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you weren't sitting down?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: That's true. I was not sitting down. I had an even better view standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that when you are standing you can see further away than when you are sitting down. From that angle you can see better than from a lower angle as --

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And there were other people to the right and to the left of you; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: The other people were sitting down. They had seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Only you were standing?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, not only me. Between the rows in the aisle people were standing, and the others were sitting down. All the seats were occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that at the time you were departing you saw some people sitting on the Sandici meadow surrounded by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in view of the season, how -- what could have been the time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It wasn't dark yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the killing in the co-operative at Kravica happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But are you sure that you saw four or five? Sorry, we have to make pauses between questions or answers. But you are sure that in the place you marked you saw four or five bodies.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in your 2004 statement, you say that you had to keep your head down on the bus.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Correct. That's right, but I still managed to see, because I looked where we were going, where they were taking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything about mutual fighting between you, by accident or intentionally, among Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You never even heard of it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see or hear about any suicides?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Suicides, I'm not sure. I think some happened, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were on the bus, and you arrived at Bratunac, and you remained on the bus through the night. That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At what points did the civilian protection give you water?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We only received water in Kasaba when we were in the schoolhouse, and we also got water in Bratunac but not while we were standing there but at a different location. When the bus stopped they give us water. In fact, they threw a hose through the window. Not everyone got water, but they pumped water through that hose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that on that bus there was no driver and no guards during that night.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those men who were guarding you at the football pitch were younger soldiers, and none of them wore the white police belt, and there were 15 to 20; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Which football field?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I skipped a bit. Before you arrived to Bratunac, at the school house?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you set out from Bratunac and what day of the week was it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think it was the 14 -- the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What time did you leave Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you headed towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it the same bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it the same number? Did it remain the same number of people on that bus? All the same people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. Those who were taken out that night never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the number of buses remained the same?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think so. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And those were buses owned by the Boksit mine?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure if all of them belonged to the Boksit mine, but one did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What time did you arrive at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We got there before dark, at dusk, late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber where the POW prison in Batkovic was. And if you are going from Bratunac towards Batkovic, would you have to go the same way, just not turn off towards Pilica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think the same road goes that way except you have to make a turn to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you help me with line 15. You said you were not sure that all the buses belonged to the Boksit mine, but one you were sure did because you saw it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How large were these buses? Were they regular buses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, it was double one, like an accordion, joint between two parts of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One of those.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you arrived and you were taken to the gym.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Somebody shot at the ceiling there; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was a volley of automatic gunfire, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And anyone who did not see the shooter could only hear the shooting; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Already on the 15th the atmosphere changed somewhat. Was it a different shift or the same, because they started asking for your jewellery, watches, money, valuables.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I think it was a different set of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They also took away your razors, knives, everything.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that point you were given to know that those among you who had relatives or friends abroad could make a phone call and tell them that they could pay ransom and buy your freedom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Weren't you also told that you could join Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While I'm looking for a reference, could you tell the Trial Chamber who Fikret Abdic was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I heard the name. I have no clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I be of assistance? Is it the case that Fikret Abdic was also a Muslim leader but of a different orientation than Alija Izetbegovic and opposed to him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not involved or interested in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you know this much: Was Fikret Abdic a Muslim leader?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Probably. How do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 22379. That's the statement we've just looked at, page 4. May I see the Serbian version of page 4. That's a passage where it says you were offered to join Fikret Abdic. Sorry, my mistake. Could we see 1D5012. 1D5012. Did you state the -- to the state commission in Tuzla in charge of collecting information about war crimes, did you make a statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then help me find the passage in this statement where it says you were offered to join Fikret Abdic. The penultimate paragraph, page 3 in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The passage Dr. Karadzic is looking for is the bottom paragraph on page 3, in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "It's true that the Chetniks asked us if any of us wanted to join Fikret Abdic, but I don't know if anybody accepted that." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't remember this, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that somebody asked for 200 Deutschmark from those who wanted to be taken to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: To Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Read this. You say maybe this happened in other rooms; correct? Page 3, after the words "Fikret Abdic," you say it's true that offer was made, but you don't remember anyone saying they charged 200 marks in exchange for transportation to Sarajevo. You say it may have happened in other rooms.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you -- do you remember this offer to join Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: They were only making fun of us and taunting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Fikret Abdic had an agreement signed with the Serbs in 1993? Why would that be a taunt, and why would they be making fun of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He said he didn't know Mr. Abdic. We'll have a break now for 15 minutes and continue more, only for 15 minutes. That's all we can make for today. And for the remainder of the hearing of today, only Judge Baird and myself will be sitting pursuant to 15 bis. We'll take a break for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Also, Mr. President, I'll have to excuse myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Well noted. Thank you. --- Break taken at 3.16 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that when you arrived, five volunteers took buckets and went down to the fountain to get water?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in another place you said that three of you volunteered, took tubs and went to a nearby brook.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Brook? What brook? Where did you find a brook?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 2379. I believe that's the documents, page 4. It's a statement given to OTP investigators. 1D5012. On page 3 you say that six of you volunteered to carry three tubs and to go to the brook.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It looked to me like a brook from up there where this water was, this sort of pond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were volunteers to get water?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To whom did you bring that water?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: The prisoners detained in the gym, the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you explain this difference, this discrepancy in the statements?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Which discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at what you said here. You said at one point that you took three tubs and in another place you said it was five buckets. Once you went to the fountain, and in another place you went to a brook.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that makes no difference to you; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It's possible that I went to fetch water twice. Maybe I went once before that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you saw some buses arrive. One or more?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I heard the sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You saw the sound. You didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also heard shooting, but you didn't -- thank you for your patience and your efforts, interpreters. Interpreters are really finding the two of us difficult. But you did not see the killing again. You only heard the shooting.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did some people provide information about family who are prepared to pay ransom for them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, a few. They were take away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And never returned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It was where they executed people on that farm, on that meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We don't have time, so we have to skip passages. People's hands were tied.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we briefly see P4347. Are you saying that before this building, five buses parked in this space?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Five buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this space fit five buses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure there were five. You mean when they were taking us for the execution or when we arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you arrived.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know. We didn't get off the bus all of us at once.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be allowed a possibility to mark something with blue pen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you would like the witness to mark on this exhibit. No. Could you repeat the number then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4349, P4349. It was admitted earlier today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were taken in groups of ten; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the place where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: When they were killing us, when -- what do you mean where I was standing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Where you were standing. Use the blue pen and mark the place where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where. It was somewhere around here in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was that, a field? Was it a field or a shrubbery?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I believe it was a shrubbery. That was a wheat field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there was no wheat.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It was either wheat or grass, but whatever it was, it was cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So groups of ten were walking. They were executed, and then they would return to fetch the other group of ten.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how long did that last?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: The whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to you, it started at 4.00 in the afternoon, and how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Until nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say that your hands were tied.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the back?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the bullet passed between your body and your arm.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how is it possible for a bullet to pass between the body and the arm if your hands are tied behind your body?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It passed through my jacket, between the body and the arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then when the shooting started, you hid under a haystack; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: That's where I was lying all the time. Another dead body fell on top of me. I stayed there the whole day, and in the evening I tried to save myself, but there was full moon and I couldn't, so I left the place sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you not state that you spent the night in a haystack in the stubble field?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: There were no haystacks. There was just some dry grass and the whole field was full of dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the haystack?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: There was no haystack. There was just dry grass scattered all over the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, where did you hide and below what?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I was in that field, in that stubble field. There was only grass. It was scattered all over the field. There were no haystacks, nothing that I could crawl into and hide beneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a wheat field, and was the wheat still there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was a wheat field or a grass field, but it was sown already. It was harvested already.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was harvested already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But there was so much of that that you could stay there a long time fully covered in that grass?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. It wasn't -- I wasn't fully covered. Only my head was covered underneath the dry grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sorry, Witness, to say that your story overlaps with some other stories by those who allegedly survived the execution.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: It is not an allegation. It is something that happened, although you say that it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that you were not there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Well, you were there then, I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's not a proper way for Mr. Karadzic to put his case to the witness. If he's going to put his case, then be specific. We've heard all week what his case about Branjevo Farm is, and I think under Rule 90(H) he should just come right out and put it to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm putting to the witness that nobody said that the execution happened there. I am claiming that there is a centre for the education of witnesses in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that the stories coincide. Some people say, Somebody fell on top of me, I heard what people were saying, then I was wandering around the Serb territory for some 15 days and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell. I'll hear from you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Again, that's not a proper way to put his case, saying that nobody has said an execution happened there. We've heard a lot of evidence that an execution happened there. So if that's Mr. Karadzic's case, then he should put it that way, but he shouldn't say that nobody else has said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If it is your case that the witness made up this story, you should put that to the witness, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying, Witness, that people said in this courtroom that the execution didn't happen here in this place. And I'm putting it to you that you were educated to describe events and that you were educated by the same people who educated other witnesses, that you made things up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember the witness -- other witness said the execution did not take place at this place, but I'll allow you to proceed, and I'll ask the witness to answer that question. Yes. Sir, could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. Were you educated to describe events in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can I tell him? He knows it only too well that things happened there, that I was there, that I was brought over there. My hands were tied. This is the execution place. Nobody can tell me that it didn't happen. It did. When you say that it didn't happen, I really don't know how to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I must say this: Dr. Karadzic is putting his case to you. He is putting his case to you. So if when you heard what he puts to you, you agree, you can say yes, you agree. If you disagree, you can say no, you disagree, but he is entitled to put his case to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't agree with what he says. Of course I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. And then when the bullet passed between your body and your arm, in other words, the bullet missed you, then you were covered with something, and then you wandered for the next 15 days around Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were captured or you surrendered and you were taken to Batkovic, to the detention camp there; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the way to Batkovic guards stopped to have a drink and the public gave you some food and some water.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: That was not on the road to Batkovic. When I was captured, we were on the bus. They did whatever they did, and then they stopped for a drink and the public gave us a drink as well, but that was not on the way to Batkovic. That was on the way to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Batkovic you were registered. Did the Red Cross register you as a prisoner of war, as a former soldier of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: We were registered. I don't know how we were registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you declare yourself? Where did they put your name?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: A detainee, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have to work for the next two or three months?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Nobody ill-treated you; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. Well, to some extent.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D5029. It should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we will keep this exhibit, as is, marked again by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document to appear, do you know that those who were taken to work there received a lot of food, plenty of food, that everybody volunteered and everybody wanted to work?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes. You couldn't survive on what we were give -- given at the camps. I also went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You volunteered; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D5029 is the document that I called up. It should not be broadcast. Is this your site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is not your site?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No. This is something that I found on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the YouTube does not have what it says here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I believe you will find this on YouTube, but this is not my site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But who's statement is this that DutchBat extracted organs from the population in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: This is something that I found on the computer and the person who stated that, his body parts were extracted. I know him. He is my relative, and as for the rest, I have nothing to do with this. This is not my site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What body part was taken from him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I don't know, he says a kidney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A kidney?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page. It seems that the two pages are not together. First of all, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't know what probative value it has at all. The witness says it's not his page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that it is, and that this is his story about Dutch soldiers. I don't know whether he created it or not, but it doesn't really make a difference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just found it on the computer, and the person who made it look like this is my page, it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, if this isn't going to be admitted, then I don't have any comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. We'll not admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5030 is the document I'm looking for. It should not be broadcast. Can this be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: This is really funny. This is a funny photo. You can do something like that. Anybody can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. But you didn't answer the question if it's you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? And if you wish to reconsider your previous decision, it will be useful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a photo from my Facebook page, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I don't see what possible relevance this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was about to ask the question to Mr. Karadzic. What was the relevance of this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a well-equipped soldier. This is what we see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, if that's the purpose for why it's being admitted then it needs a lot more foundation about when it was taken, what it's meant to depict. The photo is just in a vacuum at the moment and means nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably Mr. Witness can help us. When was this photo taken, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps five months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Five months ago?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: What are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a forest with a helmet with the military equipment? Isn't that a photo from the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I thought you were an educated man. Now I can see you're not. This is a funny photo of the kind that people publish on their Facebook pages. Anybody can do that. I don't know what else -- what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am not sorry that I am not educated to you as Facebook, but this looks like a military presentation.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, it looks like it but it's not what you think it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. We'll admit this for whatever purpose and it's for you to prove that it was taken at the time, a long time ago. Yes. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2054 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's about time to conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me see if I have any other questions. Just give me a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correction. The exhibit should be 2054 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The picture we saw is the one when you play chess online, and it's a profile that you are using on Facebook.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the conduct of the policemen who captured you, why didn't you say anything about that in your OTP statement, that lovely human conduct? Why did you keep that a secret?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: What do you mean I didn't say anything about that? You will find it in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the detail regarding the cigarettes that you were given, you didn't say anything about that to the OTP investigators, did you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I really don't know what to put to you as my last question. I simply don't have enough time.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Can I ask you something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. When I am released from the prison then you will be able to ask me.

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: I hope you will never be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is in your best interest, is it not? Can I ask you, do you know me personally, Witness? Did we ever meet?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, it is in your best interest for me not to be released from prison?

utterances.speaker: KDZ333
utterances.text: Well, in view of the number of crimes that were committed, you shouldn't be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, first, I'd like to thank the staff for their kind understanding and indulgence. I appreciate it very much. And, sir, that concludes your evidence, and on behalf of my colleagues and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague again to give it. Now you're free to go. The hearing is adjourned, and we will resume on Tuesday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of February, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.57 p.m.,
